tools.name: aggregate_telemetry
tools.title: Aggregate Telemetry
tools.description: Group spans or logs and calculate counts, error rates and durations when comparing operations or attributes.

lookback_minutes.description: Minutes before `end_time` (or now) when `start_time` is omitted, at most 43200 (30 days). Default 60, unless the tool's input description names another default.

start_time.description: Start of the window (inclusive), RFC 3339; takes precedence over `lookback_minutes`.

end_time.description: End of the window (exclusive), RFC 3339; default now.

key.description: Attribute key, e.g. `http.route`, or `service.name` for the record's service.

op.description: Comparison operator: `in` takes `values`, `exists` takes no operand and every other operator takes `value`.

value.description: Operand of every operator except `in` and `exists`. It keeps its JSON type, so the number 1 does not equal the string `1`.

items.description: A comparison operand keeps its JSON type: a number or boolean is never coerced to a string.

values.description: Operands of `in`, 1 to 256; the attribute must equal one of them.

scope.description: Where `key` is looked up: `span` or `log` for the record's own attributes (the default), `resource` for its resource attributes, such as `service.version` or `deployment.environment.name`.

items.description: One attribute predicate. It tests the record's own span or log attributes unless `scope` is `resource`; every matcher of a list must hold.

matchers.description: Attribute predicates that every matched span, resource or log must satisfy; up to 32. Omit for no filtering. discover_attributes lists the keys and values that are recorded.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of a previous call of this tool with the same filters; the cursor keeps the first page's window.

limit.description: Groups per page in `order_by` order, 1 to 200; default 20. `other` counts the groups after this page and their records.

signal.description: Which records to aggregate: `spans` (duration measures apply) or `logs`.

group_by.description: Attribute keys that define the groups, up to 4; omit for one overall group. A key is looked up in the record's attributes, then its resource, and `service.name` and `span.name` work too; a key no record carries is rejected. Each group's `key` echoes the values.

measures.description: Measures to compute per group; at least one. Accepted values: `count`, `error_count`, `error_rate` (share from 0 to 1), `duration_avg`, `duration_p50`, `duration_p90`, `duration_p95`, `duration_p99`, `duration_max` (milliseconds, spans only) and `sum:<attribute key>` for a numeric attribute. The result's `units` names the unit of each measure. Example: ["count", "error_rate", "duration_p95"].

step_ms.description: Bucket width in milliseconds for a per-group time series in `buckets`; omit for group totals only. Equal to the window length, it yields one bucket per group.

order_by.description: One of the requested measures, optionally followed by ` asc` or ` desc`. Default: the first measure, descending. Examples: `error_rate`, `duration_p95 desc`, `count asc`.

inputSchema.description: Computes numbers per group of spans or logs: counts, error counts and rates, exact duration statistics in ms or sums of a numeric attribute, optionally per time bucket. Use it for how many and how slow; list_traces finds single executions, compare_groups explains what differs between two populations, and query_metric reads pre-aggregated metrics in their own unit. Default: the last 60 minutes, 20 groups per page ordered by the first measure, descending.

tools.name: annotate
tools.title: Annotate
tools.description: Create a labeled note on a trace, span, session or failure when recording a finding, or change a note with its id and current etag; get_trace, list_sessions or get_failure_context returns it.

id.description: The annotation to change, from get_trace, list_sessions or get_failure_context; omit to create one.

etag.description: With `id`: the annotation's current `etag`, sent as If-Match.

oneOf.description: An annotation on one whole trace.

trace_id.description: The trace that holds the span.

oneOf.description: An annotation on one span of a trace.

failure_id.description: The annotated failure, e.g. from triage.

oneOf.description: An annotation on one failure, named by its `failure_id`.

target.description: What the note is attached to, required to create: a `trace`, `span`, `session` or `failure` recorded in the project. Fixed at creation.

text.description: The note, plain text, 1 to 2000 characters; required to create.

items.description: A short user-defined annotation label.

labels.description: Up to 10 labels of 1 to 64 characters each; on a change they replace the old ones. `annotation_label` filters by them.

classification.description: What the note records: `note` (the default on a create), `hypothesis`, `finding` or `rejected`.

idempotency_key.description: Without `id`: a retry key, 1 to 255 characters. Omitted, an identical create within 24 hours returns the annotation the first one created, as it is now, or a new one once that was deleted; send a new key to create another identical one. A key reused with a different body is refused while its annotation exists.

inputSchema.description: Attaches a note to a trace, span, session or failure, or with `id` and its current `etag` changes a note's text, labels or classification; the telemetry is not changed. get_trace and list_sessions return the notes on traces, spans and sessions, get_failure_context the notes on a failure and its traces, triage counts them per failure, and `annotation_label` filters list_traces and list_sessions by label. Needs the qyl:write scope; a stale etag is refused, so re-read the note and retry.

a.description: The first execution, usually the failing one.

step_ms.description: Bucket width in integer milliseconds. Omit for whole seconds that split the run's window into at most 60 buckets.

group_by.description: Attribute keys to split the result by.

key.description: Attribute key, e.g. `http.route`, or `service.name` for the record's service.

op.description: Comparison operator: `in` takes `values`, `exists` takes no operand and every other operator takes `value`.

value.description: Operand of every operator except `in` and `exists`. It keeps its JSON type, so the number 1 does not equal the string `1`.

items.description: A comparison operand keeps its JSON type: a number or boolean is never coerced to a string.

values.description: Operands of `in`, 1 to 256; the attribute must equal one of them.

scope.description: Where `key` is looked up: `span` or `log` for the record's own attributes (the default), `resource` for its resource attributes, such as `service.version` or `deployment.environment.name`.

items.description:
One structured attribute matcher. Tool inputs and saved queries carry
matchers in this form; the HTTP routes keep their `key=value` string
parameters, and a client serializes each matcher to one of them.

matchers.description: Attribute matchers a series must all satisfy.

filter.description: The stored filter, required to create; its `signal` (`traces`, `logs` or `metrics`) selects which fields apply.

idempotency_key.description: Without `id`: a retry key, 1 to 255 characters. Omitted, an identical create within 24 hours returns the saved query the first one created, as it is now, or a new one once that was deleted. A key reused with a different body is refused while its saved query exists.

inputSchema.description: Saves a named filter over traces, logs or metrics so a question can be asked again; it stores the filter, never results, and run_saved_query answers it or lists the saved queries. Without `id` it creates a saved query from `name` and `filter`; with `id` and its current `etag` it changes the fields sent, a new `filter` replacing the old one whole, and refuses a stale etag. Names are unique per project; needs the qyl:write scope.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.title: Search Logs
tools.description: Search log records and surrounding context when locating evidence linked to an execution.

span_id.description: Return only log records correlated with this span.

group_by.description: `["pattern"]` returns message templates (numbers, hex ids, UUIDs and quoted strings replaced by `#`) with their counts, most frequent first, instead of the records.

context.description: Also return up to this many records before and after each returned record from the same service and resource, in `context_logs`; 0 to 10, default 0. Not applied with `group_by`.

key.description: Attribute key, e.g. `http.route`, or `service.name` for the record's service.

op.description: Comparison operator: `in` takes `values`, `exists` takes no operand and every other operator takes `value`.

value.description: Operand of every operator except `in` and `exists`. It keeps its JSON type, so the number 1 does not equal the string `1`.

items.description: A comparison operand keeps its JSON type: a number or boolean is never coerced to a string.

values.description: Operands of `in`, 1 to 256; the attribute must equal one of them.

scope.description: Where `key` is looked up: `span` or `log` for the record's own attributes (the default), `resource` for its resource attributes, such as `service.version` or `deployment.environment.name`.

items.description: One attribute predicate. It tests the record's own span or log attributes unless `scope` is `resource`; every matcher of a list must hold.

matchers.description: Attribute predicates every returned record must satisfy; a matcher tests log attributes unless its `scope` is `resource`.

trace_id.description: Return only log records correlated with this trace.

service_name.description: Return only log records from this service.

severity_min.description: Minimum OpenTelemetry severity number: 9 info, 13 warn, 17 error.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the log body.

limit.description: Records per page, or patterns with `group_by`, 1 to 200; default 50.

session_id.description: Return only log records of this session.

lookback_minutes.description: Minutes before `end_time` (or now) when `start_time` is omitted, at most 43200 (30 days). Default 60, unless the tool's input description names another default.

start_time.description: Start of the window (inclusive), RFC 3339; takes precedence over `lookback_minutes`.

end_time.description: End of the window (exclusive), RFC 3339; default now.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of a previous search_logs call with the same filters.

inputSchema.description: Searches the window's log records, newest first, by trace, span, session, service, minimum severity, body text or matchers. Use it for the logs around one execution (pass a `trace_id` from list_traces or get_trace), or with `group_by: pattern` for the repeating message templates alone; aggregate_telemetry counts logs per attribute. Default: the last 60 minutes, 50 records per page.

tools.name: triage
tools.title: Triage
tools.description: Rank new or worsening failures, performance regressions, releases and silent services when investigating what changed, or list failures by their recorded status; the qyl MCP server's own telemetry, service qyl.mcp, is left out unless service_name names it.

lookback_minutes.description: Minutes before `end_time` (or now) when `start_time` is omitted, at most 43200 (30 days). Default 60, unless the tool's input description names another default.

start_time.description: Start of the window (inclusive), RFC 3339; takes precedence over `lookback_minutes`.

end_time.description: End of the window (exclusive), RFC 3339; default now.

key.description: Attribute key, e.g. `http.route`, or `service.name` for the record's service.

op.description: Comparison operator: `in` takes `values`, `exists` takes no operand and every other operator takes `value`.

value.description: Operand of every operator except `in` and `exists`. It keeps its JSON type, so the number 1 does not equal the string `1`.

items.description: A comparison operand keeps its JSON type: a number or boolean is never coerced to a string.

values.description: Operands of `in`, 1 to 256; the attribute must equal one of them.

scope.description: Where `key` is looked up: `span` or `log` for the record's own attributes (the default), `resource` for its resource attributes, such as `service.version` or `deployment.environment.name`.

items.description: One attribute predicate. It tests the record's own span or log attributes unless `scope` is `resource`; every matcher of a list must hold.

matchers.description: Attribute predicates that every matched span, resource or log must satisfy; up to 32. Omit for no filtering. discover_attributes lists the keys and values that are recorded.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of a previous call of this tool with the same filters; the cursor keeps the first page's window.

service_name.description: Restrict the analysis to this service (`service.name`, exact match).

environment.description: Restrict the analysis to this environment: resource `deployment.environment.name`, or the older `deployment.environment`.

limit.description: Items per page of each list (failures, regressions, releases, silent services), 1 to 50; default 10. New failures rank first, so they lead the first page.

start_time.description: Start of the window (inclusive), RFC 3339.

end_time.description: End of the window (exclusive), RFC 3339.

anyOf.description: Absolute half-open window applied by the collector.

offset_minutes.description: Minutes to shift the selected window back, e.g. 10080 for the same time a week earlier.

anyOf.description: A baseline: the selected window shifted back by `offset_minutes`, with the same length.

baseline.description: The window to compare with: `previous_window` (default), the window of equal length just before; a `{start_time, end_time}` window; or `{offset_minutes}`, the selected window shifted back.

status.description: Which failures to list by their recorded status. `open` (default) lists the failures that need attention: recorded `open`, `resolved` ones that recurred after they were resolved (`change: regressed`) and `ignored` ones whose `ignore_until` has passed. `resolved` or `ignored` list the failures recorded with that status, `all` every failure of the window.

inputSchema.description: Start of an investigation and the list of failures: the window's failures with their recorded status, new ones first and then by count, each labeled by how it changed against a baseline (new, worsening, ongoing, recovering, or regressed after being resolved), plus the operations whose error rate, p95 latency or throughput regressed, the releases first seen in the window and the silent services. The default window is the last 60 minutes, so pass a `lookback_minutes` or `start_time` that covers the incident; the baseline defaults to the window of equal length just before, and `status` defaults to `open`, the failures that need attention. A service is silent when its last span over the baseline and the window is older than the window's end minus 15 minutes or five of its usual intervals between spans, whichever is longer. The qyl MCP server's own telemetry, service `qyl.mcp`, is left out unless `service_name` names it. Explain a failure with get_failure_context and record a decision on it with update_failure_status.

tools.name: update_failure_status
tools.title: Update Failure Status
tools.description: Set a failure's status or assignee when recording triage decisions, returning the stored failure that triage then lists by status.

failure_id.description: The failure to update, from triage.

etag.description: The failure's current `etag` from triage (`status: all` lists every failure), sent as If-Match; a stale etag is refused.

ignore_until.description: With `status: ignored`, when triage shows the failure again, RFC 3339; omitted, it stays ignored. Refused with any other status.

assignee.description: Who owns the failure, at most 256 characters; omitted, the failure has no assignee afterwards.

inputSchema.description: Records a triage decision on one failure: status `open`, `resolved` or `ignored`, an optional assignee and, for `ignored`, an optional `ignore_until`. Each call replaces all three and needs the failure's current `etag`; the stored failure returns with its new etag. Triage then reports a resolved failure that recurs as `regressed` and leaves an ignored one out until its `ignore_until`, if any, passes. Needs the qyl:write scope; telemetry is not changed.

tools.name: verify_fix
tools.title: Verify Fix
tools.description: Measure failure recurrence and traffic after a change when checking whether enough evidence supports a fix.

lookback_minutes.description: Minutes before `end_time` (or now) when `start_time` is omitted, at most 43200 (30 days). Default 60, unless the tool's input description names another default.

start_time.description: Start of the window (inclusive), RFC 3339; takes precedence over `lookback_minutes`.

end_time.description: End of the window (exclusive), RFC 3339; default now.

key.description: Attribute key, e.g. `http.route`, or `service.name` for the record's service.

op.description: Comparison operator: `in` takes `values`, `exists` takes no operand and every other operator takes `value`.

value.description: Operand of every operator except `in` and `exists`. It keeps its JSON type, so the number 1 does not equal the string `1`.

items.description: A comparison operand keeps its JSON type: a number or boolean is never coerced to a string.

values.description: Operands of `in`, 1 to 256; the attribute must equal one of them.

scope.description: Where `key` is looked up: `span` or `log` for the record's own attributes (the default), `resource` for its resource attributes, such as `service.version` or `deployment.environment.name`.

items.description: One attribute predicate. It tests the record's own span or log attributes unless `scope` is `resource`; every matcher of a list must hold.

matchers.description: Attribute predicates that every matched span, resource or log must satisfy; up to 32. Omit for no filtering. discover_attributes lists the keys and values that are recorded.

limit.description: Items per page of each list the tool returns, 1 to 200; default 100. `has_more` and `next_cursor` continue the same query.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of a previous call of this tool with the same filters; the cursor keeps the first page's window.

failure_id.description: The failure to verify; its requests are the spans of its service and operation. Give exactly one of `failure_id` or `matchers`.

since.description: When the fix took effect, RFC 3339; the after window runs from here to now. Takes precedence over `release`.

release.description: A `service.version` of the failure's service (with `matchers`, of the matched requests' services) whose first recorded span marks the change, when `since` is omitted. A service that records no such version, such as a database, takes it from the services its executions run through. list_releases lists each service's versions.

min_requests.description: Requests the after window needs before the verdict can be `passed`; default 100.

min_minutes.description: Minutes after the change before the verdict can be `passed`; default 30.

verify_id.description: `verify_id` of an earlier verify_fix result: repeats that verification with its original arguments, which replace any others sent.

inputSchema.description: Checks whether a fix held: counts the failure's occurrences and its operation's requests before and after the change and answers `passed`, `failed` (it recurred), `pending` (fewer than `min_requests` requests or `min_minutes` minutes since the change) or `inconclusive`. Give exactly one of `failure_id` or `matchers` (the matched spans are the requests and their errors the failures), and a `since` time or a `release` of the failure's service whose first span marks the change; `change` names the anchor used. The before window runs from the failure's first retained occurrence (with `matchers`: from the change minus the lookback) to the change, the after window from the change to now. Repeat the check later with the returned `verify_id`.

resources.name: skill://qyl/qyl-investigate/SKILL.md
resources.title: qyl-investigate skill: SKILL.md
resources.description: Investigate a running system through the telemetry recorded in qyl, using the qyl MCP tools. Use when the user asks what qyl's traces, sessions, logs, metrics or CI runs show, for example why a request failed or was slow, what changed after a release, how MCP tools or agents performed, or whether a fix held, and when the user wants to note a finding on that telemetry, record a failure's status or save a query to run again.
